conventions.convention: N≥1, D is a nonempty finite subset of {0,1}^N, and correctness is per promised input with 0≤ε<1/2. The oracle is the standard XOR bit oracle on every address; only its calls count toward Q_ε.
Δ_i marks coordinate mismatches, F marks equal outputs, and J−F marks opposite outputs. All matrices use the same fixed ordering of D.
Adversary matrices are real symmetric, nonzero, and vanish on equal-output pairs. The denominator is max_i ||Γ∘Δ_i|| in operator norm. Signed entries are allowed; constant functions have value zero.
Filtered γ₂ uses Dirac cross pairings and minimizes the maximum of row and column sums of squared vector norms. Infeasibility has value +∞.
The consistency reflection has sign 2Π_x−I, fixes the unit start vector, and is implemented under control with two unconditional XOR queries and one clean scratch bit.

The evaluator uses U_x=(2Π_x−I)(2Δ−I), preserving both signs and chronological order. M is the least power of two at least 512A; it accepts exactly phase label zero. Witness-span reflections are input-independent nonoracle operations with no asserted efficient gate synthesis.
The finite SDP lemma assumes strict feasibility on both sides and finite optimal values; it uses real symmetric matrices and the Frobenius pairing counting both off-diagonal blocks.
Composition uses disjoint input blocks and the natural promise domain D_h; nonemptiness of D_h is explicitly required.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite nonconstant partial Boolean function, Adv±(f) equals the attained minimum of max{C_0,C_1} over finite vector families satisfying Σ_{i:x_i≠y_i}⟨v_{x,i}|v_{y,i}⟩_D=1[f(x)≠f(y)] for all distinct x,y.
For the stated finite real primal/dual SDP pair, if both feasible sets contain strict points and both optimal values are finite, then p*=d*, and both extrema are attained.
For finite-dimensional orthogonal projections Π,Δ, U=(2Π−I)(2Δ−I), and the spectral projection E_ω onto principal eigenphases of magnitude at most ω, 0≤ω≤π, Δw=0 implies ||E_ωΠw||≤ω||w||/2.

For any finite-input standard XOR bit-query algorithm using at most T queries on every branch, there is an algorithm with the same output probabilities whose evolution consists of an input-independent initial state, input-independent unitaries between exactly T unconditional calls to O_x, and a final measurement. It uses no controlled access to O_x and no more than T oracle calls.

For every promised input x, the supplied circuit realizes diag(I_H,2Π_x−I), restores its scratch qubit to zero for arbitrary control/data superpositions, and requires no controlled unknown-oracle call.

For every x∈D, the dual reflection evaluator outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3. On 1-inputs its exact common witness vector has zero phase and squared overlap with |start⟩ at least 2/3. On 0-inputs its false-positive probability is at most 3/64+1/38<1/3.
For every finite Boolean query problem and 0≤ε<1/2, Q_ε(f)≥(1/2−√(ε(1−ε)))Adv±(f).
For the stated finite partial Boolean block composition with nonempty domain, Adv±(h)≥Adv±(f)Adv±(g) and Adv(h)≥Adv(f)Adv(g).
For the sorted four-bit function specified by its eight 1-inputs, Adv(f)=5/2 and Adv±(f)>2.511486>5/2.

concerns.concern: The Statement introduces Γ and its principal eigenvector without requiring Γ to be an admissible adversary matrix, although Facts & Assumptions supplies that intended restriction. The displayed final bound is false without the opposite-output support hypothesis: take N=1, D={0,1}, f(x)=x, an exact one-query algorithm, Γ=I_2, and α=(1,0). Then W_0=W_T=1, whereas ε=0 makes the asserted final bound zero. The proof uses Γ∘F=0 in step 1.1; that essential hypothesis should be explicit in the Statement.

Proof 1.1 says the Dirac convention makes the factorization expression 'linear in each matrix factor'. It is conjugate-linear in u and linear in v; the Definition's formula and subsequent proofs use the correct convention. This sentence misdescribes the scalar behavior.

seams_checked.note: The standard-bit-query supplier gives the XOR action and involution used locally. The normal form and consistency reflection construct their control behavior with unconditional calls rather than assuming controlled unknown-oracle access.

The repeated controlled-U schedule uses M−1 calls. Circular phases are converted from radians by 2π, and the tail invocation has floor(Mω/(2π))≥20. Extension from eigenvectors to start-state superpositions follows the orthogonal spectral mixture law, also checked in its supplier.
The local circuits preserve control-first blocks, plus-on-range reflection signs, chronological product order, and the distinction between standalone and controlled scalar phase.
Cross-Gram and bra-ket formulas use the supplier's reversed Dirac pairing consistently. The isolated linearity wording defect is recorded as an owned concern.

The local Boolean interface specializes hidden-instance oracle access, per-input correctness, and worst-branch query cost. It explicitly defines its variable ε rather than relying on a supplier to provide that parameterization.
Address projectors and query-mode decompositions use finite ordered orthonormal registers. The local 1-based address labels are explicitly identified with e_{i−1}.
The scratch contract is clean restoration for every control/data superposition. Compute-phase-uncompute restores query-mode scratch, while start mode uses a |+⟩ target during both calls.
The endpoint argument uses normalized pure representatives after finite purification and coherent record retention; it makes no physical preparation or efficient synthesis claim.

Output probabilities are interpreted through terminal projections. The page asserts query complexity only and does not infer full-list polynomial-time generation or fixed-alphabet synthesis from its finite witness-span reflection.
The actual direct use is the rational bound π<22/7 from lem-qa-13-pi-rational-bounds. It correctly implies 64/π>224/11>20 in the evaluator tail calculation.
